lead.hed: Defense News: Air Force gives Boeing a $131 billion F-15 ceiling, not an order
lead.insight: Defense News, Friday: the Air Force awarded Boeing a sole-source F-15 Eagle Crest contract with a $131.23 billion ceiling to produce, modernize, and sustain F-15s for U.S. and foreign customers through 2037. The Aug. 24 War Department notice obligated $343,740 in fiscal 2026 research money at award. Orders may run through Aug. 24, 2031, with an option to 2036. The notice names foreign military sales to Japan, Israel, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Singapore, Indonesia, and Poland. It does not buy a jet on signing. The fiscal 2027 F-15EX report raises the U.S. buy to 268 aircraft through fiscal 2031.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Amy Kelley · DVIDS 9807277 · PUBLIC DOMAIN · An F-15E Strike Eagle assigned to the 85th Test and Evaluation Squadron, Eglin AFB, lands at Kadena Air Base, Japan. Date taken July 8, 2026. Caption must say July 8 file photo, not today’s contract.
lead.image_note: Official U.S. Air Force DVIDS still of an F-15E landing at Kadena. Same-subject class as the Friday F-15 Eagle Crest award — not a TPS-80, not a Roosevelt departure, not a Blue Angels air-show still, not a brand tile.

political.hed: USNI: Abraham Lincoln entered the Malacca Strait on Friday
political.insight: USNI’s Western Pacific Pulse, Friday: USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) entered the north end of the Malacca Strait on Friday, according to automatic identification system data. The Pulse is a weekly ship-movement summary, not a Navy press conference. The Navy did not publish a next port in that item.

political.hed: USNI: Navy wants a standoff aerial torpedo for carrier aircraft
political.insight: USNI, Friday: the Navy is looking to develop a next-generation standoff torpedo that can be carried by carrier-based aircraft and drones. Naval Air Systems Command released a request for information Tuesday on the Silent Anvil Air-Launched Torpedo. An RFI is a market survey, not a production buy.

political.hed: Defense News: India opens conventional missile tech to private firms
political.insight: Defense News, Friday from New Delhi: India’s defense ministry approved transferring technologies for conventional missile systems from a state-run organization to private companies. A Tuesday ministry statement called it a milestone for operational capability and less import dependence. The government did not name the missiles. Analyst Manoj Joshi said a four-day fight with Pakistan last year showed how fast stocks can run down.

tech.hed: Pentagon awards X-Bow nearly $11 million for a cheaper interceptor
tech.insight: Defense News, Thursday from Kyiv: the Defense Department awarded New Mexico’s X-Bow Systems almost $11 million under a Missile Defense Agency effort aimed at an anti-ballistic weapon for less than $750,000 a shot. X-Bow prints solid rocket motors in-house. The award funds further motor work and a first flight. The agreement calls for a prototype flight demonstration by late 2027, not a fielded round.

tech.hed: Judge Lin rules the Pentagon’s Anthropic supply-chain label illegal
tech.insight: Associated Press, Friday: U.S. District Judge Rita Lin wrote Thursday night that the Pentagon acted illegally when it designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk. Lin said the move was based on a desire to make a public example of the company for criticizing the department’s views on AI use, not on an articulable sabotage risk. Anthropic sued in San Francisco and Washington. The D.C. case is still open, so the designation is not fully lifted. The White House did not immediately comment. Nvidia’s quarter stays with Carnegie.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: Dolly Parton’s American life outlasted the fashion
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Friday: Titus Techera reads Dolly Parton’s death on Aug. 25 as the close of a distinctly Southern American life — a one-room cabin, a long marriage, hymns, and Dollywood as family entertainment rather than a lecture. The essay says she refused to politicize the feelings at the core of her songs and still built an Imagination Library that has delivered hundreds of millions of books. It is an obituary reading, not a chart claim.

watch.hed: WATCH: Marines still rehearsing a TPS-80 move in the Philippines
watch.insight: USNI, Thursday from Manila: Marine Rotational Force – Southeast Asia tested the mobility of an AN/TPS-80 Ground/Air Task-Oriented Radar. The Corps did not publish a permanent site. Thursday’s lead; Friday’s board keeps the fact on Watch.
